utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in session. Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon. Would the registrar, please call the case for today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-17-A, Miroslav Bralo versus the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Bralo, are you able to hear and to follow the proceedings in a language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like for the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter Kremer and Xavier Tracol appearing on behalf of the Prosecution. Lourdes Galicia, our case manager, is assisting us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kremer. Let me now turn to the Defence. Can you please introduce yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jonathan Cooper and Virginia Lindsay also for the Defence of Mr. Bralo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In the present case, which is pending its appeal, we know that Mr. Bralo is in custody at the Detention Unit of the United Nations in The Hague in the Netherlands. According to the provisions of Rule 65 bis(B), of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, a Status Conference on appeal is to be held at least every 120 days to allow exchanges between the parties to prepare the trial and the proceedings as quickly as possible, and to allow the person in custody to raise issues in relation to the appeal. The first Status Conference in this case took place on the 8th of May, 2005 -- 6. The scheduling order for today's Status Conference was issued on the 15th of August, 2006, and it is set today, as the date for the Status Conference, taking into account the availability of Defence counsel. Today I would like to start by turning to Mr. Bralo, and I would like to ask Mr. Bralo the following: Do you wish to raise any concerns, any issues you might have relating to your detention or to your health? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I have nothing to declare, Your Honour. Everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much, Mr. Bralo. You may be seated. With respect to the status of the appeals proceedings in this case, we first need to recall that there is a motion currently pending and the Appeals Chamber will rule on that motion once it has all the elements necessary, including the documents that the appellant has requested access to or intends to request access to. And about this matter, I would like to point amongst others -- I would like to point to the motion of 13 September, 2006, a motion currently pending before the Bench of the Appeals Chamber in the Blaskic case. Furthermore, following our decision of August 30th, 2006, the Prosecutor filed on the 8th of September, 2006, a notice stating his position about the ex parte documents listed at paragraph 20 of the above-mentioned decision. More specifically, the Prosecutor informed us that documents D239, D371 to D353, and D488 to D463, that these documents were not filed ex parte. Is that the case, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In paragraph 2 of our response, we indicate that based on our enquiries with the Registry and based on our records, those documents were not filed ex parte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. It is document 353.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: To the extent that, in asking the question, you misstated the number, I want to confirm paragraph 2 speaks of documents D239, D371 to D353, and D488 to D463.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's it, Mr. Kremer. Thank you. I will, therefore, ask the Registry to confirm that these documents were, indeed, ex parte documents and to make sure that the appellant, has had access to these documents. Mr. Kremer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecutor's position is that they were not ex parte. If they were, we have no objection to the Defence having access to the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Right. So if these documents are not ex parte documents, then the Defence will be able to have access to these documents. With respect to documents D255 and D410 to D409 what you're saying, Mr. Kremer, is that you have no knowledge about these documents? You have not had access to these documents, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We're saying that these documents have never been in the possession of the Prosecution; that the Registry numbers exist, we believe that documents may exist, but we have never had possession of them, or never had knowledge of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. From what we understand, these ex parte documents were filed by the Defence. Therefore the issue of access to these documents does not come into play for the appellant. I believe that the Defence does not agree with what I've said or maybe the information I've gained are not accurate? You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful for that. This would come as a great surprise if it were true, because I'm unaware of any documents filed by the Prosecution [as interpreted] ex parte. It would plainly help for all parties, I think, to see those relevant documents, and to be able to resolve any confusion there is immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One piece of information I would like to share with the parties, and then we can -- we will be finished with this subject. I'm talking about documents related to Ms. Lindsay. Very well. Now we can move on to the following documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: I wonder, Your Honour, just before you do, if I might make a correction to the transcript which I see at line 25 includes the words "filed by the Prosecution ex parte". That should of course should be "filed by the Defence ex parte."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's -- yes, that's right. Mr. Cooper. Yes, you're perfectly right. So the Prosecutor also stated that the remaining documents are not relevant in the current sentencing appeal. However, the Prosecutor does not object to the ex parte status of these confidential documents D204 to D202, D224 to D222, and D234 to D231, to be lifted. So it is not opposed to the ex parte status to be lifted. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you very much, Mr. Kremer. Furthermore, with respect to documents D208 to D206, D211 to D210, D216 to D213, D194 to D190, and finally D200 to D196, the Prosecutor has suggested for all information related to the former co-accused of the appellant to be redacted in order to make it possible for the ex parte status of these confidential documents to be lifted. Is that the case, Mr. Kremer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Yes, that is the position of the Prosecution, and we have provided for Your Honour and the Chamber our proposed redactions. And as you will see, the only eliminations from the documents are those in respect of the names and anything that might identify the former co-accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kremer. Can the Defence confirm that they still want to access these documents, subject to the information provided by the Prosecutor and subject to the redactions suggested by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Considering the statements that have just been made, and after having reviewed the proposals made by the Prosecutor, and the comments made by the Defence, and after consultation with the other Judges of the Chamber, we hereby decide to lift the ex parte status of the above-mentioned documents and we also decide to invite the Registry to ensure access to the Defence, access to these documents. We would like to stress that the confidential status, under-seal status of these documents remains unchanged, and that the redactions suggested by the Prosecutor have been accepted by the Chamber. Now, I would like to know if the parties have other issues they would like to raise, with respect to this particular item on our agenda. Is there anything you would like to add, Mr. Kremer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further issues? And the Defence, Mr. Cooper?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is this. Your Honour has mentioned that there is an outstanding motion by the Defence to supplement the appeal brief, and that it is not appropriate for the Appeals Chamber to rule upon that until outstanding documentation has been obtained. It occurs to me that the new material, which will be provided to the Defence pursuant to this decision, will need to be considered by the Defence. As well, the question whether there should be any additional motion to supplement the appeal brief. So it would be very helpful for the appellant to have liberty to apply to amend or to further a motion to further supplement the appeal brief, in the light of this new material. I will raise other matters, other issues about the possibility of a Rule 115 motion. Perhaps I could do that later in this hearing. But arising directly out of the disclosure that Your Honour has just ordered, there will need to be time for consideration both of its contents and whether there should be further applications of some kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cooper, of course you are perfectly entitled to file motions, including based on Rule 115. You've just mentioned it. But at this stage of the proceedings, we don't have any authorisation to give you any time limits to set. Once you have these documents, you will be able to file any motion you like, and the Chamber will then rule on these motions. Are there any other issues the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as I'm on my feet. Following on from Your Honour's observation. This is a very practical question for the appellant in this case. We have had, in this case, I'm afraid, a slow drip feed of additional information, which causes -- which raises challenges for the appellant's representatives. Each new piece of information needs to be considered in the context of the entire appeal, and we then have to consider an appropriate method of getting that material to the Appeals Chamber in the most appropriate and the briefest form. And the -- as I described it in, at one of my earlier pleadings, we haphazard approach to disclosure in this case has caused a lot of difficulty first for the appellant legal team, and I regret also for the Appeals Chamber who has had to deal with a multiplicity of pleadings on matters that might have been sorted out at a much earlier stage in these proceedings. So I'm grateful for Your Honour's observation. We of course will present any further information in the most convenient format. But our practical issue is this. Where we have incoming information which ought to be included in our submissions, is the Defence required to present a fresh pleading with each new piece of information, further multiplying the amount of paper going backwards and forwards? Or is it more sensible to produce a more consolidated pleading, firstly, in relation to the material which might supplement our brief, namely, the material which is newly disclosed from the trial record, and secondly, in relation to new material which is coming to us each day which has never been in the trial record, but which is relevant to the appeal and could be the basis for a Rule 115 motion. So the reason that I raised the question of the liberty to apply is that for exactly the reason that the Appeals Chamber does not want to rule prematurely on our motion to supplement our brief. Similarly, we don't want to, so to speak, pepper the Appeals Chamber with a series of motions which may be unnecessary, each one containing a small amount of additional information which has just come to us, whether from the Prosecution, whether from another source, or whether pursuant to Your Honour's judgement. So it seemed to us that it would be helpful to set some sort of framework and some sort of timetable for additional submissions to be made in the light of the new material that Your Honour has ordered, and which has already emerged from the Blaskic review proceedings and which may emerge in the future. And it seemed to us that that would be a sensible course, because it would assist the Appeals Chamber to be able to rule definitively on the questions that are raised by the Defence. Now, whether that is a matter capable of resolution today, I suspect it wouldn't be. But it certainly is a matter with which -- it's certainly a matter which has been raised through the normal channels, on a number of occasions. And the Defence will -- or the appellant, through his legal team, will very much wish to continue the discussion through the normal channels as to how best we can assist the Appeals Chamber. That's the point that I wanted to raise. I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Cooper. I don't know if the Prosecutor wants to take the floor about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Just to offer an observation. It seems to me that the Rules offer adequate direction to Mr. Cooper as to how he can and should proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kremer. Mr. Cooper, I believe that as part of your strategy, it's up to you to decide how you want to -- in what way you want to seize the Appeals Chamber. As far as the Appeals Chamber is concerned, well, we will answer any question you put to us. Are there any issues you would like to raise during the present Status Conference? We have covered, I believe, all of the issues we wanted to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Unless there is anything from the Prosecution side. Your Honour, as far as -- sorry, just before I embark on this point. Perhaps we might go into private session, with your leave. And the reason for that is that I would like to mention some material that ought to remain confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kremer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I know nothing of the request. I have no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much. We are sorry about those who are watching or listening to us, but we will now order private session to allow Mr. Cooper to deal with a number of issues that cannot be discussed in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So first I would like to tell Mr. Cooper that he does not have to file a first motion to get leave, which is why I told you that you don't need leave for all of this. But in your motion that you will file pursuant to Rule 115, you will state why you had to file this motion at that specific time, and the Appeals Chamber will take that into consideration and see whether your reasons are valid or not, and then will review your motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: Very well, and I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome, Mr. Cooper. No other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COOPER
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you very much. Thank you all. This status conference is now adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
